title: Collide-A-Scope: How the Internet is Fusing Our Brains and Changing Therapy, Culture and Politics

sentences.en: The low tide exposes, but I deny time for every right or wrong.
sentences.zh: 退潮显露了万物，但我拒绝为任何对错限定时间。

sentences.en: It's right on the other side, pouring fields turn beige into mazes.
sentences.zh: 就在另一边，倾泻的田野将米色变成迷宫。

sentences.en: Planetary systems go through certain phases.
sentences.zh: 行星系统会经历特定的阶段。

sentences.en: First things scither upon them as the fish walk to the foreSt.
sentences.zh: 最初的事物在其上滑过，如同鱼儿走向森林。

sentences.en: To build cities within.
sentences.zh: 在其中建造城市。

sentences.en: Retire in its incessant empire, making five fires through trees weave wires into your own.
sentences.zh: 在其永不停息的帝国中隐退，通过树木生起五堆篝火，将导线编织进你自己的经络中。

sentences.en: Hey guys, it's Joel, and welcome to the Taboo Therapy Collective PodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是乔尔，欢迎收看“禁忌疗法集体播客”。

sentences.en: Today we're going to be following up on the Mirror World series and talking about the kaleidoscope.
sentences.zh: 今天我们将继续跟进“镜子世界”系列，并聊聊万花筒。

sentences.en: How do you know that the color blue that you see is the same as the color blue that I see?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道你看到的蓝色，和我看到的蓝色是同一种颜色？

sentences.en: I mean, we both call it blue and we point at the sky and we use the same word.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们俩都管它叫蓝色，都会指着天空，用着同一个词。

sentences.en: But do we actually share the same subjective experience of that wavelength of light?
sentences.zh: 但我们对那种波长的光，真的有着共同的主观体验吗？

sentences.en: Well, some people don't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有些人并没有。

sentences.en: They might be colorblind and see it as a different color.
sentences.zh: 他们可能是色盲，看到的是不同的颜色。

sentences.en: We're just assuming that because the word matches, the experience matches too.
sentences.zh: 我们只是想当然地认为，既然词语一样，体验也一样。

sentences.en: Now this is an old philosophical puzzle and it used to be the kind of thing that you discussed in a dorm room at 2 a.m.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一个古老的哲学谜题，过去它常是那种你在凌晨两点时分在宿舍里讨论的话题，

sentences.en: and then you forgot because it didn't seem to matter.
sentences.zh: 然后转头就忘，因为这似乎无关紧要。

sentences.en: And it didn't.
sentences.zh: 曾经确实如此。

sentences.en: Or did it?
sentences.zh: 还是说其实不然？

sentences.en: We could all agree that the sky was blue, whatever blue meant to each of us privately.
sentences.zh: 我们都可以一致认为天空是蓝色的，无论对我们每个人私下来说“蓝色”意味着什么。

sentences.en: And so the word worked and communication happened and life went on.
sentences.zh: 因此这个词起作用了，交流得以发生，生活也继续运转。

sentences.en: But something has changed and that old philosophical puzzle has become the defining problem of our time.
sentences.zh: 但有些事情已经变了，那个古老的哲学谜题已经演变成了我们这个时代的决定性难题。

sentences.en: You know, we are now living through this crisis where people use the same words and they mean completely different things.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们现在正经历这样一场危机：人们使用着相同的词汇，却表达着完全不同的意思。

sentences.en: You know, freedom or Christian or a lot of big important words.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，“自由”、“基督”，或者许多宏大而重要的词汇。

sentences.en: They don't mean what you mean.
sentences.zh: 它们的含义已经不再是你所理解的那样。

sentences.en: The same sentence can be a factual claim and a tribal signal and a joke and a weapon all at once.
sentences.zh: 同一个句子可以同时既是事实陈述、群体暗号、笑话，又是一把武器。

sentences.en: You know, so you can look crazy if you point some of these things out because language has become so doubly and triply coded, you know, like computer code.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所以如果你指出其中一些现象，你可能会显得很疯狂，因为语言已经被双重甚至三重编码了，你知道的，就像计算机代码一样。

sentences.en: So, well, you can spend an hour arguing with someone online and realize at the end that you weren't even having the same conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能会花上一小时在网上和人争论，到头来却发现你们甚至根本没在聊同一件事。

sentences.en: Or maybe you don't and that changes the way that you see people.
sentences.zh: 或者也许你根本没意识到，而这改变了你看待他人的方式。

sentences.en: You know, this is a big idea, but it's not just frustrating.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是一个宏大的概念，但它不仅仅是令人沮丧。

sentences.en: It's sort of breaking politics and relationships and I would argue the mind.
sentences.zh: 它正在瓦解政治、人际关系，我甚至认为它在瓦解心智。

sentences.en: You know, this is a therapy podcast, I guess.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我猜这是一个疗法播客。

sentences.en: You know, I want to try and explain something that's happening.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我想试着解释正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: You know, why communication feels so impossible now.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，为什么现在的沟通会让人觉得如此不可能。

sentences.en: Why facts don't matter.
sentences.zh: 为什么事实不再重要。

sentences.en: And I don't mean, you know, alternative facts, facts don't matter.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是那种“另类事实”，我是说事实真的不重要了。

sentences.en: I mean, the actual facts that we think are factual do not affect us anymore in the way that we think they do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那些我们认为是事实的实际事实，已经不再以我们以为的那种方式影响我们了。

sentences.en: Our facts, not somebody else having the wrong ones.
sentences.zh: 是我们自己的事实，而不是别人掌握了错误的事实。

sentences.en: You know, we feel both simultaneously hyperconnected and utterly alone.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们同时感受到了高度的互联与彻底的孤独。

sentences.en: And I want to suggest that what we're experiencing is not just confusion.
sentences.zh: 我想提出的是，我们所经历的不仅仅是混乱。

sentences.en: It's actually a transition or an attempt to make a transition.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是一种过渡，或者说是实现过渡的一种尝试。

sentences.en: You know, it's a painful, disorienting passage between two different ways of being human.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是两种人类生存方式之间痛苦而令人迷失的过渡期。

sentences.en: And that doesn't mean that one is bad.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着其中一种是坏的。

sentences.en: It means that all of us are doing both at the same time.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们所有人都在同时经历这两种状态。

sentences.en: This is not an Us Against Them podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个“我们对抗他们”的播客。

sentences.en: It's, I don't know, if you want to be an English major and make me pick what the tension is.
sentences.zh: 这更像是，我不知道，如果你想当个文学专业学生，让我指出这里的张力所在的话。

sentences.en: I think it's an Us Against Us podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个“我们对抗我们”的播客。

sentences.en: You know, the theorist in me wants to call this the metamodern condition.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我体内的理论家倾向于称这为“后后现代状况”。

sentences.en: But I'm going to call it the digital dream time to keep it in line with Jungian psychology.
sentences.zh: 但我打算称它为“数字梦境时间”，以便让它符合荣格心理学。

sentences.en: You know, I think that understanding it is the only way that we're going to survive what's coming.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我认为理解这一点是我们从即将到来的风暴中幸存下来的唯一途径。

sentences.en: And, you know, the first part is this kind of fusion of the brain.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，第一部分就是这种大脑的融合。

sentences.en: And, you know, at Taproot, where I work, you know, we have, through Peak Neuroscience,
sentences.zh: 并且，你知道的，在塔普鲁特（Taproot），也就是我工作的地方，你知道的，我们通过巅峰神经科学（Peak Neuroscience），

sentences.en: Jay Michellany and Deanna Pizarro and Rachel and a couple other people,
sentences.zh: 杰·米切拉尼（Jay Michellany）、迪安娜·皮萨罗（Deanna Pizarro）、雷切尔以及其他几个人，

sentences.en: you know, we have this quantitative electroencephalography, you know, QEG.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们拥有这种定量脑电图，你知道的，即QEEG。

sentences.en: And it's brain mapping that, you know, is used to treat autism or dopamine disorders and anxiety,
sentences.zh: 这是一种脑部图谱绘制技术，你知道的，它被用于治疗自闭症、多巴胺失调和焦虑症，

sentences.en: different things by making different parts of the brain send information either a different way or talk more, especially more quickly, or talk less.
sentences.zh: 通过让大脑的不同部分以不同的方式传递信息，或者加强交流（尤其是加快交流速度），或者减少交流来治疗各种问题。

sentences.en: Don't talk as much.
sentences.zh: 别说那么多了。

sentences.en: Talk to another partner.
sentences.zh: 跟另一个伙伴聊聊。

sentences.en: You know, and it's this way of measuring electrical activity in the brain, wavelengths, how fast the neuron's moving and what is it sending information to.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是测量大脑中电活动、波长、神经元移动速度以及它向什么发送信息的一种方法。

sentences.en: And then seeing which areas are, you know, overactive or underactive and identifying patterns that might contribute to symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 然后观察哪些区域是，你知道的，过度活跃或活跃不足，并识别可能导致症状的模式。

sentences.en: So you can sort of bypass me.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以某种程度上绕过我了。

sentences.en: I don't have to listen to you and then diagnose you.
sentences.zh: 我不必听你倾诉然后给你诊断。

sentences.en: So your brain can just tell the machine exactly what it's doing and then the engineers can tell that to you.
sentences.zh: 所以你的大脑可以直接告诉机器它在做什么，然后工程师们就可以把这些转告给你。

sentences.en: And so I once asked, you know, when Jay and Deanna were joining, and luckily they have a good sense of humor.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一次问，你知道的，当杰和迪安娜加入时，幸运的是他们很有幽默感。

sentences.en: It's kind of hard to work with me if you don't.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有幽默感，跟我共事会有点难。

sentences.en: I was asking Jay because he was talking about how the machine worked on the idea that the brain would mimic frequencies.
sentences.zh: 我当时在问杰，因为他提到这台机器运作的原理是基于大脑会模仿频率这一理念。

sentences.en: That when the cap that does the treatment starts to put out a frequency really strongly,
sentences.zh: 当进行治疗的脑电帽开始强烈地发射某种频率时，

sentences.en: the neuron will drop the frequency it's on and say, oh, wow, you're a top-level neuron that's being a little bit louder.
sentences.zh: 神经元就会放弃它当前所在的频率，然后说：“哦，哇，你是一个声音稍微大一点的高级神经元。”

sentences.en: I'm going to mimic that frequency.
sentences.zh: “我要模仿那个频率。”

sentences.en: I'm going to do what you are doing.
sentences.zh: “我要做你正在做的事。”

sentences.en: That's how it works.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的运作方式。

sentences.en: You know, basically it's a lot more complicated than that, but that's the grossest reduction of how, you know, neuromodulation works.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，基本上它比这复杂得多，但这可以说是神经调控运作原理的最粗略简化。

sentences.en: And I asked Jay because he's super smart.
sentences.zh: 我问杰是因为他超级聪明。

sentences.en: He has a dual PhD and then Deanna's got a PhD in electrical engineering.
sentences.zh: 他拥有双博士学位，而迪安娜则拥有电子工程博士学位。

sentences.en: And Jay's a clinical psychologist in experimental research design.
sentences.zh: 杰是一位专注于实验研究设计的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: I forget what the other one was in.
sentences.zh: 我忘了他的另一个学位是什么领域的了。

sentences.en: But he's just, you know, infinitely curious people that I like being around and that kind of person.
sentences.zh: 但他只是，你知道的，那种有着无限好奇心、我喜欢与之共处的人。

sentences.en: And I was like, look, if you could keep brains alive, right, if they mimic frequency like that, you know, you're the neuroscience, it's not me.
sentences.zh: 我当时就说，听着，如果你能让大脑保持存活，对吧，如果它们真的会像那样模仿频率，你知道的，你是搞神经科学的，又不是我。

sentences.en: Like if we duct tape them together, would they start to sync up and kind of see, you know, drop redundant structures and make new networks?
sentences.zh: 就像如果我们用胶带把它们粘在一起，它们会开始同步并试着，你知道的，抛弃冗余结构并建立新的网络吗？

sentences.en: And Jay was like, oh, oh my gosh, wow, wow, what if I, yeah, oh, wow, yeah, they would.
sentences.zh: 杰当时就说：“噢，噢天哪，哇，哇，如果我，是啊，噢，哇，是的，它们会这样的。”

sentences.en: And like he had a lot of science that I still don't quite, you know, understand.
sentences.zh: 而且他讲了很多我至今仍不太，你知道的，能完全理解的科学原理。

sentences.en: But essentially, you know, they would do that if you could, you know, hypothetically pull five or six people's brains out that are still attached to the person,
sentences.zh: 但本质上，你知道的，如果你能，你知道的，假设把五六个依然连在活人身上的人脑取出来，

sentences.en: keep the brain alive, keep the person alive.
sentences.zh: 让大脑保持活性，让活人保持存活，它们就会这么做。

sentences.en: If they duct tape their brains together, where they connected, they would start to function similarly.
sentences.zh: 如果你用胶带把它们的大脑粘在一起，让它们相连，它们就会开始相似地运作。

sentences.en: You would influence each other.
sentences.zh: 你们会互相影响。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, that internet and the hyper networked reality that we are in
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道的，互联网以及我们所处的超联网现实，

sentences.en: and the infinite amount of context points, you know, reflecting that we have to swim through
sentences.zh: 还有我们必须在其中畅游的无数情境点的折射，

sentences.en: is doing something similar to that to us now, you know, that's a good metaphor for where we are.
sentences.zh: 现在正在对我们做着类似的事情，你知道的，这是对我们现状的一个很好的隐喻。

sentences.en: And, you know, the individual's minds, if you did that, it wouldn't disappear.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，如果真这么做了，个人的心智并不会消失。

sentences.en: Everybody would still be, you know, five people, four people, how many brains you want to duct tape together.
sentences.zh: 每个人依然会是，你知道的，五个人、四个人，看你究竟想用胶带把多少个大脑粘在一起。

sentences.en: But they would gravitate, you know, towards specialized roles within unified, within, you know, a unified whole.
sentences.zh: 但它们会倾向于，你知道的，在一个统一的整体内部承担起专门的角色。

sentences.en: Like, they would start to prioritize information differently so that the creature that you had made was not being as redundant.
sentences.zh: 就像它们会开始以不同的方式排列信息优先顺序，从而让你创造出来的这个“生物”不再那么冗余。

sentences.en: People would immediately serve more specialized functions, we think.
sentences.zh: 我们认为，人们会立即承担起更专门化的功能。

sentences.en: I mean, this has not been tested, obviously, outside of some kind of J-horror RPG, some kind of Japanese, like, you know, Silent Hill or Hideo Kojima or something.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这显然还没在现实中测试过，除了在某种J式恐怖RPG游戏里，某种像日式《寂静岭》或者小岛秀夫的作品里那样。

sentences.en: You know, so they would develop this new kind of individuality where they're not separate, but they were interdependent and they were offloading information to each other.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所以它们会发展出一种新型的个性：它们不再分离，而是相互依存，并彼此分担信息负载。

sentences.en: So each brain became a node in something large, would become, you know, a node in something larger than itself.
sentences.zh: 因此，每个大脑都成了某个比自身更宏大的事物中的一个节点，会变成，你知道的，比自身更宏大事物的一部分。

sentences.en: So this is science fiction, obviously.
sentences.zh: 这显然是科幻小说。

sentences.en: You know, for now, we're working on something that I hope to reveal next week, but I'm just kidding.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，目前我们正在开发某种我希望下周能揭晓的东西，但我是开玩笑的。

sentences.en: You know, we can't actually wire brains together, but we've sort of done that anyway.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们实际上没法把大脑用电线连在一起，但我们无论如何都算是做到这一点了。

sentences.en: We've just used a different kind of wire.
sentences.zh: 我们只是用了另一种不同的“电线”。

sentences.en: And so the accelerating speed of digital communication is entwining us into this vastly complex, interdependent neural network.
sentences.zh: 因此，数字通讯加速发展的速度正将我们交织成这个极其复杂、相互依存的神经网络。

sentences.en: Where every time you scroll, every time you post, every time you react to something online,
sentences.zh: 在这里，你每次滑动屏幕，每次发帖，每次在网上对某事做出反应，

sentences.en: every time you like and share this podcast with everyone in your family to make them wonder where you're getting therapy.
sentences.zh: 每次点赞并将这个播客分享给你家里的每一个人，好让他们纳闷你到底是从哪儿看的心理治疗。

sentences.en: I'm just kidding.
sentences.zh: 我开玩笑的。

sentences.en: You know, your patterns are being recognized and your frequencies are being incorporated and you're being woven together into something larger.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你的模式正在被识别，你的频率正在被纳入其中，你正被编织进一个更庞大的事物里。

sentences.en: You're offloading a certain amount of critical thinking and you're sort of picking up assumptions from something else that just become part of your wiring.
sentences.zh: 你正在分担一定量的批判性思维，并且从别的地方吸收一些假设，这些假设直接变成了你思维连线的一部分。

sentences.en: Same as a computer.
sentences.zh: 就像电脑一样。

sentences.en: And, you know, we're fusing into this singular, larger being.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们正融合成这个单一、更庞大的生命体。

sentences.en: And just a single brain can develop neuroses and this massive collection, you know, of social brain is experiencing a profound cognitive dissonance.
sentences.zh: 正如单个大脑会发展出神经症一样，这个庞大的社会大脑集合体，你知道的，正在经历深刻的认知失调。

sentences.en: I think the culture being hyperwired together has to be diagnosed en masse as it's sort of a giant brain.
sentences.zh: 我认为，被超级连线在一起的整个文化必须被作为一个巨大的大脑进行集体诊断。

sentences.en: So let's dig into it and let's see in, you know, the DSM-5TR what we would diagnose this giant collective mass of humanity with.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们深入探讨一下，看看在《精神疾病诊断与统计手册第五版修订版》（DSM-5TR）中，我们会用什么来诊断这群庞大的人类集体。

sentences.en: Not exactly, but I mean, that's the feeling.
sentences.zh: 虽然不是完全如此，但我的意思是，那就是这种感觉。

sentences.en: That's the anxiety, the polarization, the sense that reality itself has become unstable and that individuals are going crazy or something.
sentences.zh: 那种焦虑、极化，那种现实本身变得不稳定、个体正在发疯的感觉。

sentences.en: I think that is a more common perception than it was, you know, at the beginning of my life when I was, you know, 10 or 20.
sentences.zh: 我认为这比我刚到世上、大概十岁或二十岁时更成了一种普遍感知。

sentences.en: Not as many people were like, everybody's stupid.
sentences.zh: 当时可没这么多人觉得：所有人都是傻子。

sentences.en: Everybody's going crazy.
sentences.zh: 所有人都疯了。

sentences.en: You know, what's the world coming to?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这世界到底怎么了？

sentences.en: I mean, old people kind of always said that, but it was about much simpler things like that they didn't teach cursive in school or something.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，老年人过去总是这么说，但那都是关于一些更简单的事情，比如学校不教连笔字之类的小事。

sentences.en: Not the sort of things that you see today.
sentences.zh: 可不是你今天看到的这种状况。

sentences.en: And it's that, you know, collective organism that we're becoming
sentences.zh: 正是我们正在演变成的那个集体有机体，

sentences.en: that's going through this developmental crisis.
sentences.zh: 正在经历这场发育危机。

sentences.en: That's what I'm trying to analyze.
sentences.zh: 这就是我试图分析的东西。

sentences.en: You know, to understand what's happening to our communication, we need to take a step back and look at how human language has worked historically.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，为了理解我们的交流究竟发生了什么，我们需要退一步，看看人类语言在历史上是如何运作的。

sentences.en: You know, the media theorist Walter Ong, if you've ever read him, he spent his career studying the difference between oral cultures and literate culture.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，媒体理论家沃尔特·翁（Walter Ong），如果你读过他的作品的话，他毕生都在研究口头文化与识字文化之间的区别。

sentences.en: And, you know, this may sound like this academic distinction, but it's actually a pretty profound difference.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这听起来可能是一个学术层面的区别，但实际上这是一个非常深远的不同。

sentences.en: You know, in oral cultures, think of Homer's Odyssey, or a bard, you know, singing at campfires, or elders passing down tribal knowledge through stories.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在口头文化中，想想荷马的《奥德赛》，或者在篝火旁吟唱的吟游诗人，再或者是通过故事代代传承部落知识的长者。

sentences.en: Language worked in a particular way.
sentences.zh: 语言曾以一种独特的方式运作。

sentences.en: It was participatory.
sentences.zh: 它是参与性的。

sentences.en: It was performative.
sentences.zh: 它是表演性的。

sentences.en: It was mythic.
sentences.zh: 它是神话般的。

sentences.en: You know, there are the amount of books in the Odyssey is the same that there was in the Greek alphabet at that time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，《奥德赛》里的卷数和当时希腊字母表里的字母数量是一样的。

sentences.en: So that you could just sort of yell out the letter of the book of the Odyssey that you wanted the person to read.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以直接大喊出你想让对方阅读的那一卷《奥德赛》对应的字母。

sentences.en: But there wasn't a permanent record.
sentences.zh: 但当时并没有永久的记录。

sentences.en: You know, the stories existed only in the telling.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，故事只存在于讲述之中。

sentences.en: The Odyssey probably changed a lot.
sentences.zh: 《奥德赛》很可能发生过很大变化。

sentences.en: We have some evidence that it changed a lot.
sentences.zh: 我们有一些证据表明它变化很大。

sentences.en: The Bible changed a lot until it, you know, it got canonized in the Council of Nicaea.
sentences.zh: 《圣经》也发生过很大变化，直到它，你知道的，在尼西亚会议上被确立为正典。

sentences.en: A lot of these things were passed down early because that's what information was.
sentences.zh: 许多这类内容在早期都是靠口口相传流传下来的，因为那就是当时信息的形式。

sentences.en: We didn't have the idea of static information.
sentences.zh: 我们当时还没有静态信息的概念。

sentences.en: Of course, it would have to grow and change with the culture.
sentences.zh: 当然，它必须随着文化的发展而生长和变化。

sentences.en: So meaning wasn't fixed, or not exactly.
sentences.zh: 所以意义并不是固定不变的，至少不完全是。

sentences.en: It was flexible.
sentences.zh: 它是灵活的。

sentences.en: It was forged in this communal space between storyteller and audience, and the story changed depending on who was listening.
sentences.zh: 它是在讲故事的人与听众之间的这个公共空间里被锻造出来的，而且故事会根据倾听者的不同而改变。

sentences.en: And what the, you know, occasion demanded sometimes, and what felt true in that moment, or needed, true to the audience, not true to the teller.
sentences.zh: 有时根据场合的需求而变，根据那一刻感觉什么是真实的而变，或者根据听众认为真实的需求而变，而不是根据讲述者的真实需求而变。

sentences.en: You know, oral cultures thought differently because of this.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，正因如此，口头文化的思考方式截然不同。

sentences.en: Memory worked different.
sentences.zh: 记忆的运作方式不同。

sentences.en: Knowledge worked different.
sentences.zh: 知识的运作方式不同。

sentences.en: Truth itself worked differently.
sentences.zh: 真理本身的运作方式也不同。

sentences.en: It wasn't about correspondence with some external record.
sentences.zh: 它与某个外部记录是否相符无关。

sentences.en: It was about resonance with lived experience.
sentences.zh: 它关乎与生活经验的共鸣。

sentences.en: And then came writing, and eventually printing, and everything changed.
sentences.zh: 然后文字出现了，接着是印刷术，一切都改变了。

sentences.en: You know, print culture prioritized permanence.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，印刷文化把永恒性放在首位。

sentences.en: You could write something down, walk away, and it would say the same thing a hundred years later.
sentences.zh: 你可以写下一些东西，然后走开，一百年后它依然是那个样子。

sentences.en: And this shifted us more towards a literalism, an idea that we could accumulate, you know, not immediately, but this building towards this idea
sentences.zh: 这让我们更加转向字面主义，一种认为我们可以积累的观念，你知道的，不是立竿见影的，而是这种朝着某个想法的积累

sentences.en: that we could accumulate scientific fact, an objective mapping of the world, that would just sort of fill up.
sentences.zh: 即我们可以积累科学事实，对世界进行客观的测绘，而这些事实和测绘就像是被不断填满一样。

sentences.en: We used to not know what the map looked like.
sentences.zh: 过去我们并不知道地图长什么样。

sentences.en: I'm on this island.
sentences.zh: 我在这座岛上。

sentences.en: Now it's Europe.
sentences.zh: 现在这里是欧洲。

sentences.en: Now there's this other thing.
sentences.zh: 现在又有了这个别的东西。

sentences.en: Oh, now it's connected to that.
sentences.zh: 哦，现在它和那个连起来了。

sentences.en: Now the known world of land ends.
sentences.zh: 现在陆地的已知世界到头了。

sentences.en: Whoa, somebody's sailing on a ship.
sentences.zh: 哇，有人在乘船航行。

sentences.en: Here's a gap in the ocean.
sentences.zh: 这里是海洋中的一片空白。

sentences.en: Oh, the blank edges of the map are filled in.
sentences.zh: 哦，地图上的空白边缘被填满了。

sentences.en: We thought that that same thing would happen with knowledge until we, I don't know, basically knew everything.
sentences.zh: 我们曾以为知识也会发生同样的事情，直到我们——我不知道——基本上无所不知。

sentences.en: That's what the idea of literal representation
sentences.zh: 这就是字面表征的理念

sentences.en: describes,
sentences.zh: 所描述的，

sentences.en: or points you on a path towards in a way that oral representation of language doesn't.
sentences.zh: 或者说，它以一种语言的口头表征所不具备的方式，引导你走向一条道路。

sentences.en: You know, the invention of printing, the printing press, it didn't just give us books, it gave us modern science.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，印刷术的发明，印刷机的出现，它不仅带给我们书籍，还带给我们现代科学。

sentences.en: You're printing the same thing over and over and over because it doesn't ever need to change unless you have a new edition and then you sell it for $500 more
sentences.zh: 你一遍又一遍地印着完全相同的东西，因为它永远不需要改变，除非你出了新版，然后你再多收500美元

sentences.en: and call it the DSM-5TR.
sentences.zh: 并把它叫做《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》第五版修订版（DSM-5TR）。

sentences.en: I'm kidding.
sentences.zh: 我开玩笑呢。

sentences.en: Well, I'm not.
sentences.zh: 好吧，其实没有。

sentences.en: But, you know, modern law, modern bureaucracy, it gave us this idea that there's one correct interpretation of a text and that disputes can be resolved
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，现代法律，现代官僚体制，它带给我们这样一种观念：对文本只有一种正确的解释，并且纠纷可以通过

sentences.en: by pointing to what the document actually says.
sentences.zh: 指出文件实际写了什么来解决。

sentences.en: That there's sort of a canonical version out there unless the author wants you to debate or disagree and then the point of the text is that and then I guess that's the canon.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，外面似乎存在一个正统的版本，除非作者希望你去辩论或反驳，然后文本的意义就在于此，我想这就是正统吧。

sentences.en: Now this is the world where most of us were trained to navigate, that we were born into.
sentences.zh: 现在，这就是我们大多数人接受训练并学会驾驭的世界，是我们出生于其间的世界。

sentences.en: We weren't yelling out a Greek letter for Homer to read, for the bard to read that book of the Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 我们不会对着荷马大喊一个希腊字母，让吟游诗人来读《奥德赛》的那卷书。

sentences.en: We would just look it up and it would always be the same.
sentences.zh: 我们只会去查阅它，而且它永远都是一样的。

sentences.en: You know, the world of citations and fact checks but actually the dictionary defines it as
sentences.zh: 你知道的，引文和事实核查的世界，但实际上字典将它定义为

sentences.en: the world where language is supposed to be precise, where words have specific meanings, where communication is about transmitting information accurately from one mind to another.
sentences.zh: 一个语言应当精确的世界，一个词语具有特定含义的世界，一个交流意味着将信息从一个头脑准确传输到另一个头脑的世界。

sentences.en: You know, that was this new thing and so the reason I think Walter Ong is interesting and I say if I can't exploit a philosopher in a paragraph,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是个新鲜事，所以我认为沃尔特·翁（Walter Ong）很有趣的原因是，如果我不能在一段话里剥削一个哲学家，

sentences.en: I'm not going to bring him up on here.
sentences.zh: 我就不会在这里提起他。

sentences.en: I'm not going to expect you to bring anything to it but if you ever want more information about any of these guys, a lot of it is on our blog and their relevance to what I think,
sentences.zh: 我不会指望你们带来任何背景知识，但如果你想了解任何这些家伙的更多信息，很多都可以在我们的博客上找到，以及他们与我所认为的观点的相关性，

sentences.en: you know, trauma psychology, especially depth psychology.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，创伤心理学，尤其是深度心理学。

sentences.en: If you're curious, you know, I don't expect you to ever read them.
sentences.zh: 如果你好奇的话，你知道的，我从不指望你们去读它们。

sentences.en: I usually talk about somebody that I just read.
sentences.zh: 我通常谈论的都是我刚刚读过的人。

sentences.en: You know, so Walter Ong said that there's electronic media that would thrust us into an era of secondary orality where we would gain the tools of literacy,
sentences.zh: 你知道，沃尔特·翁曾说过，电子媒体会把我们推入一个次生口头性（secondary orality）的时代，在这个时代，我们将获得读写能力的工具，

sentences.en: the permanent archives and searchable databases and the ability to, you know, cite and quote and fact check.
sentences.zh: 永久的档案、可搜索的数据库，以及你知道的引用、引述和事实核查的能力。

sentences.en: You know, but we would use them more in the rhythms of an oral culture.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，但我们会更多地以口头文化的节奏来使用它们。

sentences.en: It would be participatory and performative and improvisational.
sentences.zh: 它将是参与式的、表演式的和即兴的。

sentences.en: It would return to mythology but not in our literal belief in mythology.
sentences.zh: 它将回归神话，但并不是让我们字面上去相信神话。

sentences.en: It would return more to a personal expression of the self and the function of religion, essentially,
sentences.zh: 它会更多地回归到对自我的个人表达以及宗教的功能，本质上，

sentences.en: through literal texts, not in place of them.
sentences.zh: 通过字面文本，而不是取代它们。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's what is sort of happening.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这正是正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: You know, the internet is this library and it's also a campfire.
sentences.zh: 你知道，互联网既是一个图书馆，也是一个篝火晚会。

sentences.en: You know, every conversation is simultaneously archived forever and created in the moment and we're operating in both nodes at the same time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每段对话都在被永远存档的同时又在当下被创造，我们同时在两个节点上运作。

sentences.en: And this is unprecedented in human history.
sentences.zh: 这在人类历史上是前所未有的。

sentences.en: You know, we've had people speak different languages with different words before but we've never spoken different languages with the same words.
sentences.zh: 你知道，以前我们也有过不同的人使用不同的词汇说不同的语言，但我们从来没有用相同的词汇说过不同的语言。

sentences.en: That's something that is a new phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 这是一个全新的现象。

sentences.en: The internet is this ultimate artifact of this fusion.
sentences.zh: 互联网正是这种融合的终极产物。

sentences.en: Or it's the most visible metaphor, I guess.
sentences.zh: 或者说，我想它是最直观的比喻。

sentences.en: You know, look at any successful meme.
sentences.zh: 你知道，看看任何一个成功的表情包（meme）。

sentences.en: It operates on two frequencies at once.
sentences.zh: 它同时在两个频率上运作。

sentences.en: Sometimes many more.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至更多。

sentences.en: You know, the image is usually kind of mythic or it is archetypal.
sentences.zh: 你知道，图像通常带有一种神话色彩或原型色彩。

sentences.en: It, the distracted boyfriend looking at the red or the blue-dressed girl.
sentences.zh: 比如，分心男友看着穿红衣或蓝衣的女孩。

sentences.en: You know, the woman yelling at the confused cat at the table.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那个对桌上困惑的猫大喊的女人。

sentences.en: The dog, you know, sitting in a burning room saying this is fine.
sentences.zh: 那个坐在着火的房间里说“这一切都很好”的狗，你知道的。

sentences.en: They're not really just kind of a picture that you would share that says, like, I'm happy, I'm sad.
sentences.zh: 它们其实不仅仅是你分享的一张写着“我很开心”、“我很伤心”的照片。

sentences.en: They carry this emotional resonance that transcends any particular context.
sentences.zh: 它们承载着一种超越任何特定语境的情感共鸣。

sentences.en: They usually describe a fairly complex relationship with several context points that map on to the reason you're sharing the meme.
sentences.zh: 它们通常描述了一种相当复杂的关系，包含多个语境点，这些语境点正对应了你分享这个表情包的原因。

sentences.en: The situation that you're responding to with a meme.
sentences.zh: 也就是你用表情包所回应的那种处境。

sentences.en: And so the text, meanwhile, it's hyper-literal.
sentences.zh: 因此，与此同时，文字部分是超级字面的。

sentences.en: It's a specific complaint about today's inflation rate.
sentences.zh: 它可能是对当今通货膨胀率的具体抱怨。

sentences.en: It's a precise critique of pieces of legislation.
sentences.zh: 它是对某些立法条文的精确批判。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's reference to something that happened yesterday that will be forgotten tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，它提及了昨天发生、明天就会被遗忘的事情。

sentences.en: But the meme works by fusing these two registers.
sentences.zh: 但表情包之所以奏效，正是通过将这两种语境融合在一起。

sentences.en: You know, each version is successful based on how well it does that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每一个版本的成功都取决于它将这一点做得有多好。

sentences.en: It takes your immediate specific anxiety and it links it to a timeless human pattern.
sentences.zh: 它将你即时、具体的焦虑与一个永恒的人类模式联系起来。

sentences.en: And it makes your particular suffering feel like part of something internal.
sentences.zh: 它让你经受的痛苦感觉像是某种宏大事物的一部分。

sentences.en: Eternal, sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱负，抱歉，是永恒的。

sentences.en: I didn't make my E.
sentences.zh: 我没发出那个E的音。

sentences.en: So it does what myths have always done.
sentences.zh: 所以它做了神话一直以来都在做的事情。

sentences.en: It provides a framework for making sense of experience, but it does it with this material draw, you know, from the 24-hour news cycle
sentences.zh: 它提供了一个理解体验的框架，但它是通过提取这些素材来做到的，你知道，来自24小时新闻循环，

sentences.en: where the memes spread this way.
sentences.zh: 表情包就是这样传播的。

sentences.en: And this is why they feel so satisfying to share.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么分享它们会让人感到如此满足。

sentences.en: They're not just jokes.
sentences.zh: 它们不仅仅是笑话。

sentences.en: They're tiny acts of myth-making, of mapping your context onto a giant, you know, story of others' context or, you know, archetypal context.
sentences.zh: 它们是微型的神话制造行为，是将你的语境映射到一个巨大的、你知道的、他人的语境或原型语境的宏大叙事中。

sentences.en: And they're campfire stories of the digital age and, a lot of times, literal polemic arguments at the same time.
sentences.zh: 它们是数字时代的篝火故事，而且很多时候，它们同时也是字面上的论战性辩论。

sentences.en: You know, but here's the problem.
sentences.zh: 你知道，但问题来了。

sentences.en: I mean, there are things like this that have happened before.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，以前也发生过类似的事情。

sentences.en: Like, what is it?
sentences.zh: 比如，这是怎么回事？

sentences.en: A lot of people think that the reason The Prince was written was it was like a dual intention to give the actual bad advice to the royal family, the rich family.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为《君主论》之所以被写出来，是因为它有一种双重意图，既向皇室家族、权贵家族提供真正的糟糕建议，

sentences.en: Other people think that it was like sort of to make fun of them, like something that they would take seriously, like a billionaire class, or the equivalent of a billionaire class
sentences.zh: 另一些人则认为，这有点像是在嘲弄他们，就像某种他们会认真对待的东西，比如亿万富翁阶层，或者相当于亿万富翁阶层的群体

sentences.en: would take seriously, but everybody else would be like, oh, they actually did it.
sentences.zh: 会认真对待，但其他人会觉得，哦，他们居然真的照做了。

sentences.en: And then you also have things like in the reign of Nero,
sentences.zh: 然后你也会遇到一些事情，比如在尼禄统治时期，

sentences.en: Petronius.
sentences.zh: 佩特尼乌斯（Petronius）。

sentences.en: You know, people think the Satyricon, which is this play that's incredibly lewd, very blue, all this debauchery is happening, was something that Petronius wrote
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们认为《萨蒂利孔》（Satyricon）——这部极其下流、粗俗、充斥着各种荒淫无度的戏剧——是佩特尼乌斯写来

sentences.en: to sort of like please Nero.
sentences.zh: 有点像为了取悦尼禄的作品。

sentences.en: But Nero would like it because he was gross, but also everyone else would see it and be like, oh, you're making fun of how gross he is because this is like so gross.
sentences.zh: 但尼禄会喜欢它，因为他很恶心，不过同时所有人看到它都会觉得，哦，你是在嘲笑他有多恶心，因为这实在是太恶心了。

sentences.en: This is like, you know,
sentences.zh: 这就像是，你知道的，

sentences.en: Quentin Tarantino, the Coen brothers' version of the court.
sentences.zh: 昆汀·塔伦蒂诺、科恩兄弟版本的宫廷剧。

sentences.en: And then, you know, some people say the same thing about Perpercius when we're talking about Roman poets, that his love elegies are being like kind of lewd to defy Augustus,
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，当我们在谈论罗马诗人时，有些人对普罗佩提乌斯（Propertius）也有同样的看法，认为他的爱情挽歌带有某种下流色彩来挑衅奥古斯都，

sentences.en: but at the same time talk about like love is slavery and devotion to like make fun of how Augustine has all this control.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时又谈论诸如爱情是奴役和奉献之类的话题，以此来嘲讽奥古斯都拥有何等全面的控制权。

sentences.en: And so Augustus is, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以奥古斯都，你知道的，

sentences.en: I don't think that theory holds up as well.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这个理论那么站得住脚。

sentences.en: But anyway, back to the thing.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，回到正题。

sentences.en: You know, culture doesn't evolve overnight.
sentences.zh: 你知道，文化不是一夜之间进化而来的。

sentences.en: Of course, there are examples of this happening before,
sentences.zh: 当然，以前也有过这种现象发生的例子，

sentences.en: but not at all.
sentences.zh: 但完全比不上。

sentences.en: I mean, to the extent of the shorthand we have on the internet now, where it's almost something that everyone is speaking multiple times per day.
sentences.zh: 我是说，达不到我们现在在互联网上使用的这种简写的程度，在这里，这几乎成了每个人每天都要说好几次的东西。

sentences.en: And so when everyone's speaking two languages at once, and also those are just sort of two meanings.

sentences.en: You're making random connection in the kaleidoscope of the internet.

sentences.en: And so the idea of being able to prove something, I think a lot of people are realizing, oh, man, debate club doesn't really work.
sentences.zh: 因此，关于能够证明什么的理念，我想很多人都在意识到，天哪，辩论社根本不管用。

sentences.en: What we need to do is just sort of realize like, hey, this is self-evident.
sentences.zh: 我们需要做的是意识到，嘿，这是不言而喻的。

sentences.en: This is kind of what adults know that you mean.
sentences.zh: 这正是成年人明白你的意思的那种东西。

sentences.en: This is kind of things that we think are self-evidently true.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们认为不言而喻的真理。

sentences.en: So we're moving away from that sort of like 90s West Wing, you know, debate type deal just by necessity.
sentences.zh: 所以由于必要性，我们正在摆脱那种90年代《白宫风云》式的、你知道的辩论风格。

sentences.zh: 你知道，我喜欢的一位媒体学者，

sentences.zh: 惠特尼·菲利普斯（Whitney Phillips），她谈到了

sentences.en: Poe's Law or this internet adage that it's impossible to distinguish between extreme views
sentences.zh: 波尔定律（Poe's Law），或者说这是一条互联网格言，即根本无法区分那些极端的观点

sentences.en: you know, that are parody and parodies of those views that the internet sort of said.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们到底是讽刺，还是对这些观点的讽刺，互联网似乎就是这么说的。

sentences.en: I guess kind of like the satiricon, you know, we're going to make this like a hundred times billion bigger version of what I'm, what I, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想有点像《萨蒂利孔》，你知道的，我们要把这个搞得比我所做的、我所，你知道的，

sentences.en: of you.
sentences.zh: 比你的版本大上千百亿倍。

sentences.zh: 我要做出这种夸张，或者将你所有的信仰推向它们的终极、

sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然，我在节目中收到的一些电子邮件，你知道的，我没有抱任何幻想。

sentences.en: Most people don't like it.

sentences.zh: 也许他们自己也分不清。

sentences.zh: 而且这并不是，这种模棱两可并不是系统漏洞。

sentences.zh: 你知道，对某些人来说，这是个功能。

sentences.en: They get to pretend like they believe everything and then depending on what happens, they get to pick the one that is preferable.
sentences.zh: 他们得以假装自己相信一切，然后根据发生的情况，挑选出那个对自己更有利的立场。

sentences.en: They get to pretend that that's what they always thought.
sentences.zh: 他们可以假装那就是他们一直以来的想法。

sentences.en: So, you know, think about the political paradox of the last decade.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，想想过去十年的政治悖论。

sentences.en: Like when Donald Trump got elected in 2016, you know, the political right recognized a societal void of meaning, vulnerable, and they projected their need for this modernist,
sentences.zh: 比如唐纳德·特朗普在2016年当选时，你知道的，政治右翼识别出了社会意义上的真空，极其脆弱，他们将自己对这种现代主义、

sentences.en: heroic myth onto this guy.
sentences.zh: 英雄式神话的需求投射到了这家伙身上。

sentences.en: And yeah, there was some going on with that, with Clinton too.
sentences.zh: 没错，克林顿身上其实也发生过类似的事情。

sentences.en: It just, I guess, wasn't as popular of a myth.
sentences.zh: 只是，我想它没有那么受欢迎，没能成为那么流行的神话。

sentences.en: There really wasn't much to either of those candidates other than what you projected onto them.
sentences.zh: 除了你投射到他们身上的东西之外，这两个候选人其实并没有太多实质内容。

sentences.en: I think that's what made a lot of people upset, the people that weren't doing much projecting.
sentences.zh: 我想这正是让许多人感到不安的原因，那些并没有进行太多投射的人。

sentences.en: And so, you know, there's these elevated 80s and 90s characters that got elevated into, you know, emperors or, you know, wise sages or projections they probably didn't deserve.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，有些80和90年代被拔高的角色被提升为了，你知道的，皇帝，或是智慧的先知，或者说承担了他们可能并不配得上的投射。

sentences.en: And the political, you know, the liberals, you know, attempted to counter that mythic projection by using these tools of postmodern literalism.
sentences.zh: 而政治上的，你知道的，自由派，你知道的，试图通过使用这些后现代字面主义的工具来对抗这种神话投射。

sentences.en: They wanted to deploy fact checkers and have companies that told you whether or not the information on the meme was accurate.
sentences.zh: 他们想要部署事实核查员，并让一些公司来告诉你表情包里的信息是否准确。

sentences.en: Like you could police the internet in real time.
sentences.zh: 就像你能实时监管互联网一样。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: didn't work out by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，根本行不通。

sentences.en: Those companies folded.
sentences.zh: 那些公司都倒闭了。

sentences.en: And they pointed out that, you know,
sentences.zh: 他们指出，你知道的，

sentences.en: Trump's wealth wasn't dead so he wasn't actually rich or something.
sentences.zh: 特朗普的财富并没有缩水，所以他其实没那么有钱之类的话。

sentences.en: But I mean, hell, the guy's sitting on a gold throne for most of his life.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，见鬼，这家伙大半辈子都坐在金王座上。

sentences.en: He looks pretty rich to me, you know, so this failed as a project.
sentences.zh: 在我看来他挺有钱的，所以这个计划可以说是失败了。

sentences.en: All of these ways to sort of take Trump apart because you can't really defeat myth with fact checking.
sentences.zh: 所有这些试图解构特朗普的方法，因为你无法真正用事实核查来战胜神话。

sentences.en: That's not the role that myth plays.
sentences.zh: 那不是神话所扮演的角色。

sentences.en: And so the American electorate
sentences.zh: 因此，美国选民

sentences.en: has repeatedly rejected, you know, the sterile procedural language of modern liberalism because it lacks any compelling mythic vision of the future.
sentences.zh: 一再拒绝现代自由主义那枯燥僵化的程序语言，你知道的，因为它缺乏任何引人注目的未来神话愿景。

sentences.en: You know, the Democrats brought spreadsheets to a mythological battle.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，民主党在一场神话般的对决中带了一堆电子表格。

sentences.en: And if you check page, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果你翻到，你知道的，

sentences.en: 14 of the website, you'll actually see that she thinks something about that.
sentences.zh: 网站的第 14 页，你就会发现她对此有某种看法。

sentences.en: That just didn't work.
sentences.zh: 这根本行不通。

sentences.en: And they spoke on this literal register while their opponents, you know, were speaking on both.
sentences.zh: 他们在使用这种字面层面的语言，而他们的对手，你知道的，两者兼顾。

sentences.en: They were more mimetic and they won.
sentences.zh: 他们更具拟态性，而且他们赢了。

sentences.en: Whether or not whatever was true, they won.
sentences.zh: 不管那些事是不是真的，他们赢了。

sentences.en: And this isn't about one party being smarter than the other because it goes back and forth and there were a lot of things that both campaigns did wrong and both sides of the aisle
sentences.zh: 这并不是说哪个政党比另一个更聪明，因为这总是反复拉扯，两党竞选团队都做错了很多事，而且两派

sentences.en: now still do wrong both parties.
sentences.zh: 现在仍然在犯错，两党都是。

sentences.en: And I don't mean wrong like I disagree with it or disagree with most of it.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是那种我不同意或者不同意其中大部分内容的错误。

sentences.en: I mean wrong like it's clueless, it doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是那种毫无头绪、根本行不通的错误。

sentences.en: They don't understand what's effective right now.
sentences.zh: 他们不明白现在什么才有效。

sentences.en: And it's about understanding the linguistic terrain we're operating in.
sentences.zh: 这是关于理解我们所处的语言环境。

sentences.en: You know, you can't defeat the myths of the modern with literalism of the postmodern.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你无法用后现代的字面主义来战胜现代的神话。

sentences.en: You have to synthesize both and make a new thing.
sentences.zh: 你必须将两者融合，创造出一样新东西。

sentences.en: And you have to be able to speak mythically and literally at the same time with full awareness of what you're doing in each register.
sentences.zh: 你必须能够同时以神话和字面的方式进行交流，并且充分意识到自己在每个层面上的所作所为。

sentences.en: And if you're working with younger people in therapy, this is something that older therapists, middle-aged therapists, need to learn to do because it's a big part of doing therapy
sentences.zh: 如果你在心理治疗中与年轻人打交道，这是年长治疗师、中年治疗师需要学会的事情，因为这是进行心理治疗的重要组成部分

sentences.en: with a younger population.
sentences.zh: 针对年轻人群体。

sentences.en: It's a language that they speak.
sentences.zh: 这是他们说的一种语言。

sentences.en: It's not really a language I speak at home, but it's a language that I speak in therapy with some people.
sentences.zh: 这其实不是我在家里说的语言，但这是我在治疗中与某些人交流时会用的语言。

sentences.en: And at this point, a reasonable person might object.
sentences.zh: 此时，一个理性的人可能会提出异议。

sentences.en: Hasn't it always been like this?
sentences.zh: 难道事情不一直都是这样的吗？

sentences.en: Haven't humans always, you know, fused facts and myths together?
sentences.zh: 人类难道没有一直把，你知道的，事实和神话融合在一起吗？

sentences.en: Haven't politicians always wrapped policy in patriotic symbols?
sentences.zh: 政客们难道没有一直用爱国符号来包装政策吗？

sentences.en: You know, hasn't politics always been a religion or a football team?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，政治难道不一直是一种宗教或一支足球队吗？

sentences.en: Haven't religious leaders always, you know, enforced mythical belief through literal rules?
sentences.zh: 宗教领袖难道没有一直通过，你知道的，字面规则来强化神话信仰吗？

sentences.en: I mean, yeah, but that's a fair critique.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，是的，但这确实是一个合理的批评。

sentences.en: You know, human nature hasn't changed that much, like I say in therapy pretty often.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，正如我经常在治疗中说的那样，人性并没有太大改变。

sentences.en: If these problems go all the way back to the Bronze Age, if they're in the Bible, don't count on them getting solved in your life.
sentences.zh: 如果这些问题一直追溯到青铜时代，如果它们存在于《圣经》中，就别指望它们在你这一生中能得到解决。

sentences.en: While they exist, because they've been with us for a long time.
sentences.zh: 只要它们存在，因为它们已经伴随我们很久了。

sentences.en: People have been speaking out of both sides of their mouth since language began.
sentences.zh: 自从有了语言以来，人们就一直是两面三刀的。

sentences.en: What's changed is the medium in the past and the speed.
sentences.zh: 改变的是过去的媒介和速度。

sentences.en: Marshall McLuhan would say that the medium is the message.
sentences.zh: 马歇尔·麦克卢汉会说，媒介即讯息。

sentences.en: You know, in the past, the mythic register and the literal register were somewhat separate and the mythic belonged to the church and the theater and the festival and the campfire
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在过去，神话层面和字面层面在某种程度上是分开的，神话属于教堂、剧院、节日和篝火

sentences.en: and the culture and the literal belonged to the courthouse and the laboratory and the newspaper and the bureaucracy.
sentences.zh: 以及文化，而字面则属于法院、实验室、报纸和官僚机构。

sentences.en: And you knew which mode you were in based on the context.
sentences.zh: 你根据上下文就知道自己处于哪种模式。

sentences.en: Not just of what was being said, but where you were.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅取决于所说的话，还取决于你身处何地。

sentences.en: And the architecture of social life kept them somewhat distinct and you could sort of go to one when you needed one and the other for something else.
sentences.zh: 社会生活的结构使它们在某种程度上保持截然不同，当需要其中一个时你可以去找它，需要另一个时则找另一个。

sentences.en: The internet has forced both modes into the exact same text box.
sentences.zh: 互联网强行把这两种模式塞进了同一个文本框里。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I know that if we never invented the internet that churches probably still would have started to play politics and science more and, you know, the science
sentences.zh: 是的，我知道，如果我们从未发明互联网，教堂可能还是会开始更多地涉足政治和科学，而且，你知道的，科学

sentences.en: would have maybe continued to evolve until it sort of became this existential religion or something.
sentences.zh: 可能也会继续发展，直到某种程度上变成这种存在主义的宗教或别的什么。

sentences.en: I've heard those critiques too.
sentences.zh: 我也听过这些批评。

sentences.en: I don't, that's not really what I mean.
sentences.zh: 我不是，这并不是我真正的意思。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，

sentences.en: it's not the same thing as the same platform where you file your taxes is where you encounter apocalyptic memes or the same feed that contains peer-reviewed research, you know,
sentences.zh: 这与你报税的平台和遭遇末日模因的平台不是同一个，或者说包含同行评议研究的同一个信息流里，你知道的，

sentences.en: having tribal war cries and selling you pyramids to sharpen razor blades or the same 280 characters have, you know,
sentences.zh: 有着部落的战斗口号，向你兜售金字塔来打磨剃须刀，或者同样的 280 个字符拥有，你知道的，

sentences.en: the same language as like the 13-year-olds on the internet and the White House or, you know, vice versa.
sentences.zh: 和互联网上的 13 岁孩子以及白宫一样的语言，或者，你知道的，反之亦然。

sentences.en: You also see a whole lot of teenagers talking about geopolitics in a way that it's like, what?
sentences.zh: 你还会看到一大群青少年以一种让人觉得“什么鬼”的方式谈论地缘政治。

sentences.en: There's a lot of cross-contamination and that sort of made everything a different cultural node, a different context point.
sentences.zh: 这里有很多交叉污染，这使得一切都变成了一个不同的文化节点、一个不同的语境点。

sentences.en: And this isn't just a faster version of what we've always done, though.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是我们一直在做的事情的加速版本。

sentences.en: The speed is a big part of it.
sentences.zh: 速度是其中很大一部分。

sentences.en: But the speed of the architecture have created something qualitatively new.
sentences.zh: 但速度与架构共同创造了一种质的飞跃。

sentences.en: When everyone with a smartphone is forced to be a curator of cultural, you know, just to participate in a basic conversation, that's a psychological toll
sentences.zh: 当每个拥有智能手机的人都被迫成为文化的策展人，你知道的，仅仅为了参与一场基础的对话，这就会带来心理上的代价

sentences.en: that causes a lot of anxiety.
sentences.zh: 并引发极大的焦虑。

sentences.en: And there's another factor, the surveillance and profit infrastructure that's been put on top of all of this.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个因素，即叠加在这一切之上的监控与盈利基础设施。

sentences.en: You know, the platforms aren't neutral pipes.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这些平台并不是中立的管道。

sentences.en: A lot of the memes are about that.
sentences.zh: 很多模因都与此有关。

sentences.en: They're making fun of the platform that they have to use or talking about the limitations of it like surveillance.
sentences.zh: 它们在嘲笑自己不得不使用的平台，或者讨论诸如监控之类的局限性。

sentences.en: They're designed to maximize engagement.
sentences.zh: 它们旨在最大化用户的参与度。

sentences.en: And engagement is maximized by content that triggers strong emotional responses.
sentences.zh: 而参与度是通过触发强烈情感反应的内容来最大化的。

sentences.en: Which means the algorithms are systematically amplifying the most mythic, the most tribal, the most emotionally charged content.
sentences.zh: 这意味着算法正在系统性地放大那些最具神话色彩、最具部落属性、最具情绪煽动性的内容。

sentences.en: And while suppressing the measured, the nuanced, and the merely informative, this is also not an original or new argument.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，它们在压制那些深思熟虑的、充满细微差别的以及纯粹提供信息的内容，这也并非一个原创或崭新的论点。

sentences.en: We just sort of at this point agree that that's happening.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在这一点上达成了一种共识，即这种现象正在发生。

sentences.en: But nobody knows how to stop it.
sentences.zh: 但没有人知道该如何阻止它。

sentences.en: The fused brain isn't just performing organically.
sentences.zh: 融合的大脑不仅仅在有机地运转。

sentences.en: It's being shaped by incentive structures that reward the most destabilizing forms of communication.
sentences.zh: 它正被那些奖励最具颠覆性沟通形式的激励机制所塑造。

sentences.en: We are making the collective brain sick.
sentences.zh: 我们正在让集体大脑变得生病。

sentences.en: The cognitive dissonance isn't accidental.
sentences.zh: 认知失调并非偶然。

sentences.en: And I think that it's profitable.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这很赚钱。

sentences.en: Panic is profitable.
sentences.zh: 恐慌很赚钱。

sentences.zh: 但来回摆动，没有哪个立场是稳固的。

sentences.en: And the oscillation is not an end state.
sentences.zh: 而且这种摇摆并不是最终状态。

sentences.en: It's a phase.
sentences.zh: 它只是一个阶段。

sentences.en: The pendulum swings until it finds this new equilibrium, or it's not a pendulum.
sentences.zh: 钟摆会一直摆动，直到找到这个新的平衡点，或者说它根本不是一个钟摆。

sentences.en: The fused brain doesn't have to be a monster, the collective organism doesn't have to be pathological, and the dreamtime doesn't have to be a nightmare.
sentences.zh: 融合的大脑不必成为怪物，集体有机体不必走向病态，梦境时间也不必是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: But whether or not it becomes something beautiful or something terrible or something just more human or sort of in a cycle of both of those things, we contain both.
sentences.zh: 但它最终会变成美好的事物、可怕的事物，还是更具人性的事物，亦或是两者兼有的循环，这一切我们都包含其中。

sentences.en: You know, it depends on how we navigate the transition.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这取决于我们如何度过这个过渡期。

sentences.en: We have to kind of endure tension, we have to find some way to clean up collective trauma, and we have to learn to sit with uncertainty, to step into the unknown with some
sentences.zh: 我们必须承受某种张力，必须找到某种方法来清理集体创伤，并且必须学会安于不确定性，带着某种超越科学、

sentences.en: kind of more than scientific and also more than spiritual faith in something, in ourselves, in a future that is bigger or better than this.
sentences.zh: 也超越精神层面的信念迈入未知，去相信某种事物、相信我们自己、相信一个比这更宏大或更美好的未来。

sentences.en: For a long time,
sentences.zh: 长期以来，

sentences.en: objectivities could stay separate.
sentences.zh: 客观性是可以保持独立的。

sentences.en: You know, your reality is over there and their reality is over there, so go where you belong.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你的现实在那边，他们的现实在那边，所以去你该去的地方吧。

sentences.en: Different populations inhabiting different worlds, each, you know, internally coherent, each reflecting its own assumptions back to itself.
sentences.zh: 不同的人群居住在不同的世界里，每个世界都是内部自洽的，每个世界都在向自身反射着各自的假设。

sentences.en: I mean, these bubbles floated alongside of each other without touching, and the mirrors faced their own mirrors and reflected endlessly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些气泡互不接触地漂浮着，镜子面对着各自的镜子，无休止地反射着。

sentences.en: You could go your whole life without seriously confronting the fact that other people lived in a completely different factual universe from you.
sentences.zh: 你可能一辈子都不会去认真面对这样一个事实：其他人生活在一个与你完全不同的事实宇宙中。

sentences.en: That's one of the things that I want to be real clear is not new.
sentences.zh: 我要明确指出的一点是，这并不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: But those bubbles couldn't stay separate forever.
sentences.zh: 但这些气泡不可能永远保持独立。

sentences.en: You know, the crises that we face are now too large to be contained in a single bubble, you know, because these things are starting to collide based on the way that we've
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们现在面临的危机太大了，无法被限制在一个单独的气泡里，因为由于我们对世界进行了超级网络化连接，这些事物开始发生碰撞，

sentences.en: hyper-networked the world, and we can't hide from each other in the way that we used to be able to based on, you know, where we went in our free time and who we talked to.
sentences.zh: 我们再也无法像过去那样，通过选择去哪里消磨业余时间和跟谁说话来彼此躲藏了。

sentences.en: That's why I'm calling this the kaleidoscope.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我称之为万花筒。

sentences.en: You know, these parallel realities that could coexist through mutual avoidance and being forced together now, and they're grinding against each other like gears that don't mesh.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这些曾经通过相互回避而共存的平行现实，现在被迫交织在一起，它们像不啮合的齿轮一样互相摩擦。

sentences.en: You know, they're teeth that don't fit.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它们是不匹配的齿轮。

sentences.en: They're mechanisms that are clashing.
sentences.zh: 它们是互相冲突的机制。

sentences.en: And the whole apparatus is kind of shuddering until it figures out a new way to run, a new type of lubricant.
sentences.zh: 整个机器都在震颤，直到它找到一种新的运转方式、一种新型的润滑剂。

sentences.en: You know, in a kaleidoscope, mirrors create beautiful patterns, and they reflect fragments into symmetry.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在万花筒中，镜子创造出美丽的图案，它们将碎片反射成对称的形状。

sentences.en: But what happens when the mirrors themselves start moving, when they're no longer fixed in place, but they're sliding and crashing and breaking?
sentences.zh: 但是，当镜子本身开始移动时会发生什么？当它们不再固定在原地，而是在滑动、碰撞和破碎时会发生什么？

sentences.en: The patterns shatter, and the fragments collide, and the reflections become collisions.
sentences.zh: 图案破碎，碎片碰撞，反射变成了冲突。

sentences.en: And that's where we are.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们目前的处境。

sentences.en: The separate realities can't stay separate, and the material world won't let them go, and the crises are too big, too fast, too indifferent to respond to our constructions, and a
sentences.zh: 各自独立的现实无法继续保持分离，物质世界也不会放过它们，危机太巨大、太迅速、太冷漠，以至于无法仅靠我们的构建来应对，而且很多时候，

sentences.en: lot of times we don't even notice them until they're gone.
sentences.zh: 直到它们消失，我们甚至都没有注意到它们。

sentences.en: The 24-hour news cycle has become a 24-second news cycle.
sentences.zh: 24小时新闻循环已经变成了24秒新闻循环。

sentences.en: You can feel this in every conversation that goes wrong, in every, you know,
sentences.zh: 你可以在每一次出错的对话中感受到这一点，在每一个，你知道的，

sentences.en: place where you feel disconnected from things like family, or community, or therapy, or medical things, or art, or community spaces that just either aren't there
sentences.zh: 你觉得自己与家庭、社区、心理治疗、医疗、艺术或社区空间等事物脱节的地方，而这些地方要么根本不存在，

sentences.en: or don't feel right anymore.
sentences.zh: 要么感觉不再对劲了。

sentences.en: You know, this grinding is painful, and it's disorienting, and it feels like the end of something.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这种摩擦是痛苦的，会让人迷失方向，并且感觉就像是某种事物的终结。

sentences.en: Um, but here's what grinding does.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但摩擦的作用是这样的。

sentences.en: It wears things down that don't fit.
sentences.zh: 它会磨损掉那些不合适的东西。

sentences.en: It removes the parts that don't make the thing run.
sentences.zh: 它会除掉那些阻碍机器运转的部件。

sentences.en: Grinding does make things fit back together, and the parallel realities have to come back together somehow, because we have to find things that we all think are
sentences.zh: 摩擦确实能让事物重新契合在一起，平行现实必须以某种方式重新汇合，因为我们必须再次找到那些我们都认为是

sentences.en: self-evident, that we all agree on again.
sentences.zh: 不证自明的事物，找到我们都能重新达成共识的东西。

sentences.en: Even if we can't agree on how things work, we need to start by agreeing on what the goals are.
sentences.zh: 即使我们无法就事物如何运作达成一致，我们也需要从就目标达成一致开始。

sentences.en: And this is kind of a brittle hope, you know, a brutal hope, you know, living in this collision.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是一种脆弱的希望，你知道的，一种残酷的希望，你知道的，就生活在这场碰撞中。

sentences.en: You know, the bubbles were never sustainable.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这些气泡从来都不是可持续的。

sentences.en: The parallel objectivities were always a temporary condition, so what comes after the collision?
sentences.zh: 平行的客观性一直都只是一种暂时的状态，那么碰撞之后会发生什么？

sentences.en: The separate perspectives that we've had have been reflecting each other for decades now, you know, building power before they collided, potential energy.
sentences.zh: 我们所拥有的那些相互分离的视角，几十年来一直在彼此反射，你知道的，在它们碰撞之前积蓄力量，形成势能。

sentences.en: You know, mirror facing a mirror, you know, each one is confirming its own assumptions.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，镜子面对着镜子，每一个都在通过反射确认自己的假设。

sentences.en: By seeing them reflected back.
sentences.zh: 通过看到它们被反射回来。

sentences.en: But reflection without contact is just narcissism.
sentences.zh: 但是没有接触的反射只是自恋。

sentences.en: You know, it's each bubble admiring its own constructed reflection.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是每个气泡都在欣赏自己构建出的倒影。

sentences.en: And the collision breaks the narcissism.
sentences.zh: 而这场碰撞打破了这种自恋。

sentences.en: It forces contact with what's outside.
sentences.zh: 它迫使我们与外界进行接触。

sentences.en: We may have lost the ability to be as avoidant as we wish we could be.
sentences.zh: 我们可能已经失去了像自己希望的那样去逃避的能力。

sentences.en: You know, the metamodern condition isn't just oscillation anymore, it's collision.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，超现代状态不再仅仅是摇摆，而是碰撞。

sentences.en: And the poles were swung between, they're crashing together.
sentences.zh: 我们曾在其间摇摆的两极，现在正猛烈撞击在一起。

sentences.en: And in that crash, something is going to give.
sentences.zh: 而在那场撞击中，总会有所妥协或发生变化。

sentences.en: A kaleidoscope is turning, and the mirrors are moving, and the patterns are shattering.
sentences.zh: 万花筒在转动，镜子在移动，图案在粉碎。

sentences.en: And what we build from these fragments is the new picture.
sentences.zh: 而我们从这些碎片中构建的，就是全新的图景。

sentences.en: And I hope it can hold us.
sentences.zh: 我希望它能容纳我们。

sentences.en: I hope it can hold us really tight.
sentences.zh: 我希望它能紧紧地拥抱我们。

sentences.en: And I hope it can make us feel safe.
sentences.zh: 我希望它能让我们感到安全。

sentences.en: The biggest step that I see is the recognition that trauma treatment is self-evidently necessary.
sentences.zh: 我看到的最大的步子，是认识到创伤治疗是显而易见的必要之举。

sentences.en: But before that, we are traumatized.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，我们已经受创了。

sentences.en: We're being traumatized by this.
sentences.zh: 我们正因此而受到创伤。

sentences.en: You know, it's not a luxury, it's a foundation.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这不是一种奢侈，而是基石。

sentences.en: It's a right.
sentences.zh: 这是一项权利。

sentences.en: And because trauma fuels the blind spots, it makes these things worse.
sentences.zh: 正因为创伤助长了盲区，它让事情变得更糟。

sentences.en: It makes us less likely to ever solve them.
sentences.zh: 它让我们更不可能去解决这些问题。

sentences.en: Trauma is why we built the bubble.
sentences.zh: 创伤正是我们建造气泡的原因。

sentences.en: Trauma is why we defend representations that don't connect anything real.
sentences.zh: 创伤正是我们捍卫那些与现实毫无关联的表象的原因。

sentences.en: The collective organism is sick.
sentences.zh: 集体有机体病了。

sentences.en: It's traumatized.
sentences.zh: 它受到了创伤。

sentences.en: And the parallel realities, the grinding gears, are these responses groaning at collective scale.
sentences.zh: 而那些平行的现实、那些摩擦的齿轮，正是这种痛苦在集体层面的悲鸣。

sentences.en: We have to learn how to actually live together.
sentences.zh: 我们必须学会真正地生活在一起。

sentences.en: Not to manage each other.
sentences.zh: 而不是互相管理。

sentences.en: Not to avoid each other.
sentences.zh: 也不是互相回避。

sentences.en: Actually live together.
sentences.zh: 而是真正地生活在一起。

sentences.en: And Western history is largely the story of how we managed avoiding parts of self even when we had to live in proximity.
sentences.zh: 西方历史在很大程度上讲述了这样一则故事：即便我们不得不近距离生活，我们是如何设法回避自我的一部分的。

sentences.en: Connection without internal avoidance.
sentences.zh: 没有内部回避的连接。

sentences.en: That's the task.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的任务。

sentences.en: You can't connect with others unless you understand the parts of yourself.
sentences.zh: 除非你理解了自省的部分，否则你无法与他人连接。

sentences.en: And you can't face parts of yourself that you can't tolerate.
sentences.zh: 而你无法面对那些你无法容忍的自我部分。

sentences.en: Internal avoidance has become external avoidance.
sentences.zh: 内部回避已经变成了外部回避。

sentences.en: We need to see ourselves as multiplicities, not unified selves.
sentences.zh: 我们需要将自己视为多重性的存在，而不是单一统一的自我。

sentences.en: It was always a fiction.
sentences.zh: 那本来就只是一种虚构。

sentences.en: We need to stop splitting through emotion.
sentences.zh: 我们需要停止通过情绪来进行分裂。

sentences.en: We can hold our own multiplicity.
sentences.zh: 我们完全可以容纳自身的多重性。

sentences.en: The parallel realities are not just political.
sentences.zh: 平行现实不仅仅是政治问题。

sentences.en: They're psychological.
sentences.zh: 它们也是心理问题。

sentences.en: And the external fragmentation mirrors the internal fragmentation.
sentences.zh: 外部的破碎映射了内部的破碎。

sentences.en: You can't fix one without addressing the other.
sentences.zh: 不解决其中一个，你就无法修复另一个。

sentences.en: The internal system is the external system.
sentences.zh: 内部系统就是外部系统。

sentences.en: That's what the collective brain metaphor of the dreamtime gives us.
sentences.zh: 这就是梦境时间的集体大脑隐喻带给我们的启示。

sentences.en: You know, what we build from these fragments depends on whether we can finally stop avoiding ourselves.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们从这些碎片中构建出什么，取决于我们能否最终停止逃避自己。

sentences.en: don't like are just there.
sentences.zh: 那些我们不喜欢的东西就摆在那里。

sentences.en: And they're just there like it's raining outside.
sentences.zh: 它们就那样存在着，就像外面在下雨一样。

sentences.en: Or they're just there like there's a mountain in your way.
sentences.zh: 或者它们就那样存在着，就像你面前挡着一座山一样。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter what you think about it.
sentences.zh: 你怎么想并不重要。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter what you feel about it.
sentences.zh: 你怎么感觉并不重要。

sentences.en: Those things are real.
sentences.zh: 那些东西是真实存在的。

sentences.en: We didn't choose this.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们的选择。

sentences.en: But the collision is happening whether we want it or not.
sentences.zh: 但无论我们愿意与否，碰撞正在发生。

sentences.en: And the only question is whether we participate consciously, whether we bring the witness consciousness, the dual language fluency, the shamanic navigation to the collision, or
sentences.zh: 唯一的问题是，我们是有意识地参与其中——是将见证者的意识、双重语言的流畅性以及萨满式的导航带入这场碰撞，

sentences.en: whether we just get ground up in the gears because we refuse to see reality inside of us and inside of other people.
sentences.zh: 还是仅仅因为拒绝看清内在于我们以及内在于其他人身上的现实，而在齿轮中被粉碎。

sentences.en: That's where it always was.
sentences.zh: 现实一直都在那里。

sentences.en: Build a bridge.
sentences.zh: 去搭建一座桥吧。
